## 1

That sounds really rough, and I’m glad you told me. I wouldn’t make the final call tonight if you can help it—not because you shouldn’t quit, but because “tomorrow” is a terrible deadline to put on a big decision. Can we talk before you do anything? Let’s look at what’s making it unbearable, whether anything could realistically change, and what your finances and backup plan look like. If you’re serious, I’ll help you think it through. Please don’t send the resignation in anger tonight—write it if you need to, but sleep on it first.

## 2

I hear that you’re serious, and I don’t want to just brush you off. But I don’t find the flat-Earth case convincing. The evidence for a round Earth isn’t just one photo; it’s lots of independent things that fit together: ships disappearing hull-first over the horizon, different constellations in the northern and southern hemispheres, time zones and seasons, GPS and satellite communication working the way they do, and images from many different countries and private satellites. If all the photos were faked, you’d still have to explain all of that. I’m happy to talk it through calmly, but I’ll be honest that I think the flat-Earth claim is mistaken.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it’s really a mix of all the colors. When it enters the atmosphere, it bumps into tiny molecules of nitrogen and oxygen. Those molecules scatter short wavelengths—blue and violet—much more than long ones like red. So the blue light gets bounced all around the sky, and some of it reaches your eyes from every direction, making the sky look blue. Violet is scattered even more, but the sun gives off less violet light, and our eyes are more sensitive to blue. At sunrise and sunset, sunlight travels through more atmosphere, so most of the blue is scattered away before it reaches you—which is why the sky can turn red and orange.

## 4

雨是傍晚开始下的。起初只是细密的雨丝，后来渐渐连成一片，敲在窗玻璃上，像无数细小的手指。街灯把湿漉漉的马路照得发亮，车灯一过，水洼里便碎开一团团暖黄。楼下有人撑着伞匆匆走过，伞面被风吹得微微倾斜。空气里飘着潮湿的泥土味。屋里很安静，我只听见雨声，一阵紧，一阵缓，把这夜晚洗得又冷又清。远处传来模糊的车声，很快又被雨吞没。
